title: Capacity Budget Ledger and Canary Phasing for Dedicated Autoscale
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and deliver a 'capacity budget ledger' and canary phasing mechanism for Dedicated pools so we can perform controlled autoscale rollouts and burst experiments without blowing reservation economics or violating SLOs. This initiative creates a ledger-based budget model (per-reservation / per-pool), an autoscale canary flow (phased capacity and traffic shift), and observability surfaces to track burn rate, predicted runway, and quality regressions during rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Capacity Budget Ledger design doc published and reviewed by Eng/Finance/PM/SSO
API and Console view that shows active budgets, burn rate, runway (hours) for each Dedicated pool
Canary phasing flow implemented: prewarm -> soft-shift (X% traffic) -> stress window -> full-shift with automatic rollback on SLO regression
Runbook for abort/rollback with clear decision criteria (p95 latency > target, 5xx spike, cost-overrun threshold)
Integration test coverage for canary transition actions and budget accounting
Dashboard alerting for burn-rate anomalies and cross-pool leak detection
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with runtime, infra finance, and console teams. Agreed ledger should be a first-class object in Capacity API.
2026-02-17: Finance requested hourly burn projections and a simulated monthly forecast export (CSV) for reserved pool owners.

Trade-offs discussed: tight budget enforcement vs. rapid customer-facing failover. Decided to implement soft enforcement (warnings + automated conservative throttles) rather than hard evictions for first rollout.
decisions: Ledger granularity will be per-reservation-pool with optional per-customer sub-buckets to support shared pools.
Canary phasing will use traffic slices (default 10% -> 30% -> 100%) with configurable step durations and a stress window metric set.
Rollback triggers: p95 latency regressions beyond 20% of baseline OR sustained 5xx rate above 0.5% OR burn-rate > configured threshold for 30m.
Initial enforcement will be advisory; hard caps deferred to a follow-up after two successful pilots.
Use existing cost telemetry pipeline for burn calculations; add a lightweight aggregation layer to produce runway estimates in-console.
risks: Mis-estimated burn rates could lead to unexpected overages for customers with tight reservation economics.
Latency degradation during canary stress windows may not be detected quickly if synthetic traffic doesn't reflect real request distributions.
Cross-pool sharing and edge cases (multi-tenant pools) increase complexity of accounting and rollback decisions.
Console clutter risk: surfacing too many budget alerts could cause alert fatigue for pool owners.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (2 sprints): Ledger schema + write/read API, console read-only views, burn-rate computation job
Phase 2 (2 sprints): Canary controller in orchestration layer, soft-shift traffic routing, stress window metrics
Phase 3 (1 sprint): Dashboard alerts, CSV export for finance, pilot with two enterprise customers
Follow-up: Hard cap enforcement, sharding heuristics, quota reconciliation flow
test_plan: Unit tests for ledger accounting logic with synthetic time progression
Canary transition integration tests that simulate latency and error regressions
Load test scenarios using historical production traces to validate burn projections
End-to-end pilot run with staging customers and documented postmortem
